svg.title: Nearby-vehicle application: pairing from similar sensor fingerprints
svg.desc: Devices in two nearby cars measure acceleration, rotation, and air pressure. Local processing creates similar binary fingerprints used as fuzzy passwords. An RRSS-based fPAKE establishes a shared key when their Hamming distance is within the tolerance. FastZIP is prior work; RRSS replaces the robust secret sharing component in its fPAKE implementation. The sensor traces and bit strings are illustrative.
svg.text: Device pairing from shared physical context
Adapted application scenario • Similar sensor fingerprints serve as fuzzy passwords.
TWO NEARBY CARS ON THE SAME ROAD
Secure communication between the two cars for exchanging traffic data
Replaces RSS in the FastZIP codebase
FastZIP: Fomichev et al., MobiSys 2021. RRSS: Ameri & Blocki, ACM CCS 2026.
Adapted two-car illustration; original FastZIP evaluates intra-car pairing. Traces and fingerprints are illustrative.
*Comparison as reported in the RRSS paper. Sensor context and online guessing determine pairing security.
